findings.passage: The Voting Rights Protection Act would have enhanced voter ID requirements, and provided a free ID to ensure everyone could meet the requirement; ensured uniformity in the conduct of elections across counties; provided for early voting and correcting some defects on mail-in ballots; and offered counties more time to process registration applications and count ballots.
findings.note: Statement issued in his name after the governor vetoed House Bill 1300. He describes what the bill would have done: stronger voter ID rules with a free ID, uniform county procedures, early voting, fixes for mail-ballot defects and more processing time.

findings.passage: This is a definite step back; however, I will continue to work with my colleagues to answer the demands of voters to ensure safe, secure and accessible elections in Pennsylvania.
findings.note: Closing line of the same statement on the veto of House Bill 1300.

findings.passage: Furthermore, the governor today also vetoed funding in the budget for a Bureau of Election Audits within the Department of the Auditor General.
findings.note: Same statement. He also objects to the veto of budget money for a Bureau of Election Audits.
